rationale: Consolidate the duplicate Transform 66 Outside the Beltway project record into I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC, the legal concessionaire and operator. Meridiam's official opening release expressly states that the 66 Express Lanes Outside the Beltway project is also known as Transform 66 Outside the Beltway, and FHWA identifies I-66 Express Mobility Partners LLC as the private partner for that same 22.5-mile DBFOM concession. Ferrovial's audited 2025 Form 20-F confirms that Cintra continues to hold 55.7%, with Meridiam Infrastructure S.a.r.l. at 29.75% and I-66 Blocker (APG) at 14.55%. Current Ferrovial, Meridiam, VDOT, and concessionaire materials continue to describe the operating project and the Cintra-Meridiam-APG consortium, and no later APG or Meridiam exit, pending sale, or change of control was found through August 8, 2026. Preserve APG and Meridiam as separate active manager ownership periods, correct their current disclosed vehicles and stakes, add the project trade names as aliases, refresh the operating description and website, attach direct evidence to each retained milestone, and retire the duplicate project record through the canonical redirect workflow. Cintra's controlling interest is stated in the description and evidence but is not added as a manager ownership period because Cintra/Ferrovial is outside the supplied 100-manager census universe and no matching organization dependency exists in the approved task snapshot.

beforeImage.name: I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC
beforeImage.description: I-66 Express Mobility Partners is the concessionaire for the 66 Express Outside the Beltway project in Northern Virginia. Its users are commuters, freight operators, and other motorists traveling the I-66 corridor between the Capital Beltway and Prince William County. The project follows a long-term public-private concession model under which the consortium designed, financed, built, operates, and maintains priced express lanes and related roadway improvements. Public materials describe a $3.7 billion, 22.5-mile managed-lanes project delivered under a 50-year agreement with the Virginia Department of Transportation. The lanes opened in 2022 and the project includes highway, transit, and corridor-improvement components across one of the region's most congested corridors. The consortium is publicly described as including Cintra, Meridiam, and APG, while current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

afterImage.name: I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC
afterImage.description: I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC is the private concessionaire and operator of the 66 Express Outside the Beltway managed lanes in Northern Virginia, also known as Transform 66 Outside the Beltway. Under a 50-year DBFOM agreement with the Virginia Department of Transportation through 2066, the company financed, delivered, operates, and maintains a 22.5-mile corridor from I-495 to Route 29 in Gainesville. The approximately $3.7 billion project includes two express lanes and three rebuilt general-purpose lanes in each direction, interchange upgrades, more than 4,000 park-and-ride spaces, transit funding, and 18 miles of shared-use path. The full corridor opened ahead of schedule in November 2022. Ferrovial's audited 2025 filing reports Cintra at 55.7%, Meridiam Infrastructure S.a.r.l. at 29.75%, and I-66 Blocker (APG) at 14.55%.

milestones.event: VDOT and I-66 Express Mobility Partners signed the comprehensive agreement for the 50-year Transform 66 Outside the Beltway DBFOM concession.
I-66 Express Mobility Partners reached financial close with equity investors including APG and Meridiam Infrastructure North America Fund II.
Cintra completed the acquisition of an additional 5.704% interest from John Laing, increasing its controlling stake in the I-66 concession to 55.704%.
The western nine-mile section of the 66 Express Lanes opened ahead of schedule between Gainesville and Route 28 in Centreville.
The full 22.5-mile 66 Express Outside the Beltway corridor opened to traffic ahead of schedule.
